title: My sleep app recorded two hours of whispering 😴
style_prompt: cinematic horror film still, dark moody blue-teal grade, one bright light source, well exposed, 35mm film grain, realistic, no text, no watermark, no faces
hook_text: At 7:02 a.m. my sleep app had recorded two hours of someone whispering my name.

scenes.narration: At 7:02 a.m. my sleep app had recorded two hours of someone whispering my name.
I use a sleep tracker. It records snoring, sleep talking, any noise in the night. Usually it shows a flat quiet line.

shots.prompt: bedside table with a phone, a glass of water and a lamp, soft morning light, no person

scenes.narration: That morning the graph was one solid block. Two hours long. From 3:14 to 5:14 a.m. A voice. Not mine.

shots.prompt: dark bedroom doorway slightly open, thin cold light spilling in, no person

scenes.narration: I pressed play. A whisper. Low. Slow. My name. Over and over. Like someone testing the sound of it.

shots.prompt: phone lying on a pillow with a glowing waveform, dim bedroom, no text, no face

scenes.narration: I skipped forward. Still whispering. I skipped again. The voice was louder now. Closer to the microphone. Closer to my pillow.

shots.prompt: rumpled pillow with a head-shaped dent in the dark, a phone glowing beside it, no person

scenes.narration: At 4:40 the whisper changed. It stopped saying my name. It said, she is awake. She is pretending.

shots.prompt: dark bedroom at night seen from above the bed, a phone glowing, no face

scenes.narration: I had slept through all of it. Or I had not. I remembered lying very still with my eyes shut. Feeling someone lean in.

shots.prompt: dark bedroom corner with a tall pale shape of light on the wall, no person

scenes.narration: The last second of the recording was my own voice. Very quiet. It said, please stop.

shots.prompt: smartphone on a wooden table, glowing blue screen, dark room, no person

scenes.narration: So tell me. Do you sleep tonight with the app on, or leave the house?
